note.explanation: Elements, compounds and mixtures differ in how their particles are made and joined. Elements contain one kind of atom; compounds contain elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio; mixtures contain substances mixed without chemical bonding.
examples: Water (H₂O) is a compound: hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
Salt water is a mixture: salt and water are mixed, and the salt retains its identity.
note.checkAnswer: A mixture has components that are not chemically bound together and can be separated by physical methods.
note.simple: An element has one kind of atom. A compound has different elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio. A mixture has different substances together but not chemically joined.
note.checkQuestion: How can the components of a mixture be separated?
note.title: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
steps: Check whether the sample contains one kind of atom, chemically combined elements, or mixed substances.
For a compound, look for chemical combination in a fixed ratio.
For a mixture, remember that its components retain their properties and can be separated physically.
note.answer: A mixture is a sample of matter containing more than one type of element or compound mixed together in any ratio.

options: A pure substance containing the same kind of atoms
Different substances chemically combined in any ratio
Two or more substances mixed in a fixed ratio
A pure substance that can always be separated physically
rationales: Correct: an element is a pure substance containing the same kind of atoms.
Incorrect: chemical combination describes a compound, and compounds form in fixed ratios.
Incorrect: substances mixed in any ratio describe a mixture.
Incorrect: an element cannot be broken down by ordinary chemical reactions.

options: Its components retain their identities and properties
Its elements are always present in any ratio
It can be separated only by chemical reactions
Its properties are always different from its components
mcqs.stem: Which statement is a property of a mixture?
rationales: Correct: each component of a mixture retains its identity and specific properties.
Incorrect: a mixture may be in any ratio, but this option incorrectly describes its elements as having a fixed identity in that ratio.
Incorrect: mixtures can be separated by physical methods.
Incorrect: this is a property of compounds, not mixtures.

options: The atoms of its elements combine in a fixed ratio by weight
Its components can be separated by physical methods
It contains only one kind of atom
Its components always retain their original properties
mcqs.stem: What distinguishes a compound from a mixture?
rationales: Correct: the elements in a compound combine in a fixed ratio by weight.
Incorrect: physical separation is a feature of mixtures.
Incorrect: one kind of atom describes an element.
Incorrect: mixture components retain their properties; compound properties differ from those of its elements.

options: Water
Salt dissolved in water
A sample of rock
A mixture of sand and iron filings
mcqs.stem: Which of these is a compound?
rationales: Correct: water is a compound made from hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed ratio.
Incorrect: salt dissolved in water is a mixture.
Incorrect: rock is given as an example of a heterogeneous mixture.
Incorrect: sand and iron filings are mixed, not chemically combined.

options: The components are chemically bound together
The components are not chemically bound and can be separated physically
The components must be present in a fixed ratio
The mixture has properties different from all its components
mcqs.stem: Which statement best describes how the components of a mixture are held together?
rationales: Incorrect: chemical bonding between elements is characteristic of compounds.
Correct: mixture components are not chemically bound and can be separated by physical methods.
Incorrect: a fixed ratio is a feature of compounds, not mixtures.
Incorrect: the textbook states that mixture properties are the sum of those of its components.

options: A solution of common salt in water
Water
Hydrogen chloride
Ammonia
mcqs.stem: Which is an example of a homogeneous mixture?
rationales: Correct: a solution of common salt in water is given as a homogeneous mixture.
Incorrect: water is a compound.
Incorrect: hydrogen chloride is a compound.
Incorrect: ammonia is a compound.

options: It can be broken into simpler particles by ordinary chemical reactions
It is represented by a symbol when it exists as atoms
It always exists as independent molecules
It is made from different elements in a fixed ratio
mcqs.stem: Which statement about elements is correct?
rationales: Incorrect: an element cannot be broken down into simpler particles by ordinary chemical reactions.
Correct: an element existing as atoms is represented by a symbol, such as Na or Ca.
Incorrect: some elements exist as atoms, while gaseous elements may exist as molecules and noble gases are monoatomic.
Incorrect: different elements combined in a fixed ratio describe a compound.

options: The properties of a compound are always different from those of the elements forming it
A compound's components can always be separated by physical methods
A compound contains only one type of element
A compound has no fixed ratio of its elements
mcqs.stem: Which statement about compounds is correct?
rationales: Correct: the properties of a compound are always different from those of the elements from which it is formed.
Incorrect: a compound is broken into its constituent elements by a chemical reaction.
Incorrect: a compound is formed from two or more atoms of different elements.
Incorrect: the elements in a compound combine in a fixed ratio by weight.

examTips: A board question may ask you to differentiate between elements, compounds and mixtures. Write clear points in a table for easy marking.
Include the key distinctions: kinds of particles, fixed ratio, chemical combination, properties, and how components can be separated.
Give the textbook examples where relevant: water as a compound, salt solution as a homogeneous mixture, and rock as a heterogeneous mixture.

hints: Think of elements that can occur naturally without being chemically combined with other elements.
Examples include gold, silver and copper.
yourTurn.question: Which elements are found in pure state on Earth?
solution: Some elements can occur in nature in an uncombined, or native, state.
Examples include gold, silver and copper.
yourTurn.answer: Examples include gold, silver and copper.

hints: The question asks for elements that are scarce, not the most abundant elements.
Gold, silver and platinum are examples of elements found in small amounts.
yourTurn.question: Which elements are present in very small amounts on Earth?
solution: Some elements are present in very small amounts compared with the common elements of Earth's crust.
Examples include gold, silver and platinum.
yourTurn.answer: Examples include gold, silver and platinum.

steps.why: A compound is made when atoms of different elements combine chemically.
steps.text: Water is a compound formed from hydrogen and oxygen.

steps.why: A fixed ratio by weight is a defining feature of a compound.
steps.text: In water (H₂O), hydrogen and oxygen are present in a fixed ratio of 1:8 by weight.

steps.why: The elements in a compound can be separated by a chemical reaction, unlike the components of a mixture.
steps.text: A compound can be broken into its constituent elements by a chemical reaction.

example.question: Use the textbook description to explain why water is a compound.
example.answer: Water is a compound because hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio of 1:8 by weight.

explain.title: Elements
explain.body: An element is the simplest form of matter. It is a pure substance containing the same kind of atoms. It cannot be broken down into simpler particles by ordinary chemical reactions. When an element exists in the form of atoms, it is represented by a symbol, such as Na for sodium and Ca for calcium.

explain.title: Compounds
explain.body: A compound is a pure substance. It is formed by the chemical combination of two or more atoms of different elements. These atoms combine in a fixed ratio by weight. A compound can be broken into its constituent elements by a chemical reaction, and its properties differ from those of the elements forming it.

explain.title: Mixtures
explain.body: Mixture is an impure compound. A sample of matter having more than one type of elements or compounds mixed together in any ratio, is called a mixture. Its components retain their identities and specific properties, are not chemically bound together, and can be separated by physical methods.

explain.title: Homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures
explain.body: A mixture may be homogeneous or heterogeneous. A solution of common salt in water is homogeneous, while a sample of rock is heterogeneous. The properties of a mixture are the sum of those of its components.

mistakes: Do not say that the components of a mixture are chemically combined; they are not chemically bound and can be separated by physical methods.
Do not confuse a fixed ratio in a compound with the any-ratio composition of a mixture.
Do not write that a compound has the same properties as its elements; its properties are different.
Give a suitable example when asked to compare homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures.
